docs.text: MAR-40 data harmonization and standardization Authors: Farnoosh Abbas Aghababazadeh Contact: farnoosh.abbasaghababazadeh@uhn.ca Description: Development of standardized data processing and harmonization procedures, standard operating procedures (SOPs), quality control frameworks, and reproducible Snakemake workflows for clinical and molecular data in the MAR-40 immuno-oncology research program. Overview MAR-40 is a collaborative immuno-oncology research program that integrates heterogeneous clinical and molecular datasets across participating institutions. This repository supports consistent and reproducible data curation, standardization, harmonization, and quality control across collaborating sites. The project aims to: Standardize clinical and molecular metadata using common data dictionaries and controlled vocabularies. Harmonize cohort-specific fields for cancer type, treatment, response, survival outcomes, and molecular assays. Document source-to-standard mappings, provenance, quality-control decisions, and unresolved discrepancies. Support reproducible computational workflows and downstream immuno-oncology biomarker analyses. Set Up Prerequisites Pixi is used to manage the project environment. If it is not yet installed, follow the Pixi installation instructions . Installation Clone the repository and navigate to the project directory: ```bash git clone https://github.com/bhklab/mar40-data-harmonization.git cd mar40-data-harmonization ``` Set up the project environment: bash pixi install For detailed setup instructions and reproducible workflows, see the Usage . Documentation View the full documentation at MAR-40 data harmonization . Document Purpose Data Curation SOP Step-by-step clinical and molecular data curation, processing, and harmonization procedures. Data Dictionary Standardized fields, definitions, units, and permitted values. Data Sources Cohort provenance, source documentation, and data access. Quality Control Validation, missingness, consistency checks, and QC reporting. Usage Instructions for running workflows and reproducing outputs. Development Notes Technical notes and development decisions. Data curation and harmonization workflow Data acquisition and provenance: Identify source cohorts, publications, datasets, access permissions, and source versions. Clinical metadata curation: Review patient/sample identifiers, demographics, disease classifications, treatments, responses, and survival endpoints. Molecular data preparation: Document assay modalities, processing methods, and molecular annotations. Harmonization: Apply the shared data dictionary, controlled vocabularies, and documented source-to-standard mapping decisions. Quality control: Check missing values, duplicated records, conflicting fields, assay links, and unresolved mappings. Reproducible outputs: Produce standardized files, QC summaries, and provenance records using version-controlled workflows. Follow the Data Curation SOP for detailed procedures and Quality Control for checks and review expectations. Data Organization Directory Contents data/rawdata/ Original source data and source-specific documentation. data/procdata/ Processed and harmonized clinical and molecular data. data/results/ Generated summary tables, figures, and analysis outputs. See the Raw Data README and Processed Data README for directory-specific conventions. Data access: Do not commit private or controlled-access patient-level datasets to a public repository. Store restricted data only in approved environments; commit only documentation, code, and appropriately authorized example or synthetic data. Reproducibility Collaborators should follow the shared SOP and dictionary, use version-controlled scripts and configurations, document mapping decisions and unresolved cases, review QC results, and record input provenance and software versions. These practices allow data preparation steps to be reviewed and rerun consistently across participating sites.

docs.text: MAR-40 Data Curation and Harmonization SOP Version: v1.0 Scope: Participating MAR-40 teams curating clinical and molecular immuno-oncology cohorts Document owner(s): Farnoosh Abbas Aghababazadeh Effective date: November 20, 2026 Repository location: docs/data_curation_SOP.md Related documents: Data dictionary · Data sources · Quality control · Usage Status: Version 1.0 establishes the MAR-40 data curation and harmonization procedures agreed upon by the collaborating teams at UCL, McGill University, and University Health Network (UHN). Changes and cohort-specific deviations are documented through version control and the review process described below. 1. Purpose and expected outcome Establish a transparent, reproducible procedure for acquiring, curating, harmonizing, validating, and documenting clinical and molecular data contributed to MAR-40. Apply common data definitions across institutions while retaining the meaning and provenance of the original source records. At the end of curation, each cohort should have, where the source data permit : A versioned source inventory and provenance record. Harmonized patient- and/or sample-level clinical metadata with documented identifiers. Standardized treatment, disease, response, survival, and assay descriptors. Processed molecular data with documented units, reference annotations, and processing methods. An explicit linkage between clinical records and molecular samples; an MAE object when appropriate. A quality-control (QC) report, mapping log, unresolved-issues register, and reproducibility manifest. Principle: Do not invent missing clinical measurements, infer unsupported mappings, or silently discard records. An absent or unverified variable is not a negative observation. 2. Roles, accountability, and data stewardship Role Responsibility Contributing site / cohort curator Identify approved sources, perform source-level curation, record provenance and mapping decisions, run QC. Site scientific/data lead Review clinical meaning, data-access constraints, and flagged ambiguities; approve site-specific submissions. MAR-40 harmonization team Maintain shared schemas, mapping rules, versioned workflows, and cross-site comparability checks. Designated scientific reviewer Resolve decisions that change endpoint meaning, response definitions, tumor taxonomy, or assay comparability. Review rule: A curator must not independently resolve a clinically consequential ambiguity by guesswork. Record it as Needs review and escalate to the site's designated reviewer. Maintain a change log for decisions applied across cohorts. 2.1 Data protection and permitted sharing Classify data as Public , Controlled access , or Private , based on actual source permissions and institutional agreements. These labels describe access arrangements, not data completeness. Use only approved institutional environments for controlled/private patient-level information. Do not commit restricted source data, credentials, or direct identifiers to GitHub. Keep a shareable repository containing code, documentation, mappings permitted for distribution, test fixtures, and approved synthetic examples. Before sharing any outputs across borders or organizations, confirm the applicable ethics approval, data-transfer agreement, institutional policy, and export permissions. Technical reproducibility does not itself grant permission to share data. Where data cannot move between sites, execute the approved workflow locally and share only explicitly permitted metadata, reports, or aggregate results. 3. Overall workflow Register a cohort and verify access. Establish source, citation, scope, permissions, and local contact. Inventory source files. Preserve raw inputs; record file versions, assays, units, and identifiers. Curate clinical metadata. Standardize identifiers, demographics, disease, therapy, response, and survival fields. Process or import molecular profiles. Document RNA and DNA methods and preserve assay-specific information. Harmonize annotations and vocabularies. Apply versioned mappings for tumor types, drugs, endpoints, and features. Integrate sample-to-patient relationships. Produce interoperable tables and MAE components, when applicable. Perform automated QC and scientific review. Resolve or explicitly flag inconsistencies. Release curated outputs. Version outputs and record input provenance, code commit, software environment, and reviewer decisions. 4. Cohort registration and source inventory Create one entry per cohort in the registry described in Data sources . Record at least: Information Expected record Cohort identifier Stable project-specific cohort ID; avoid naming collisions across sites. Source Publication/DOI, accession, study documentation, provider, or approved local location. Site and curator Contributing organization, responsible curator, contact or team. Access status Public / Controlled access / Private, with permission or agreement reference. Study design Trial/observational; treatment arms and timepoints if documented. Data availability Clinical, RNA, SNV, CNA, other; raw vs processed; counts and formats. Source revision Download/release date, original filename, checksum where permitted. Use restrictions Distribution, reuse, location, and retention restrictions. Completion check: The origin and access status of every input file are traceable. Retain the original data as received; do not overwrite rawdata during standardization. 5. Clinical metadata curation 5.1 Define record granularity and identifiers Distinguish patient , specimen/sample , assay , treatment episode , and timepoint . Repeated samples from one patient must not be counted as distinct patients. Use site-appropriate pseudonymous identifiers and preserve an approved, protected linkage when necessary. patientid : stable within the defined cohort and uniquely linked to the relevant patient. sampleid : stable sample identifier; one patient can have multiple sample IDs. treatmentid : treatment regimen identifier when supported by the source. sample_timing : documented pretreatment/on-treatment/post-treatment or other timepoint classification; retain original dates/labels in controlled source records if permitted. When patient IDs can overlap between cohorts, identify a patient by cohort + patientid for summaries unless a verified cross-cohort identity linkage exists. Check: One molecular sample should resolve to an appropriate clinical patient record; any many-to-many or uncertain match requires documented review. 5.2 Required fields versus unavailable fields The MAR-40 target schema includes standardized fields such as patientid , treatmentid , response , tissueid , survival_time_os , survival_time_pfs , survival_unit , and the corresponding event indicators. Preserve these as the target schema where relevant; a cohort is not automatically ineligible because the source lacks a field. Domain MAR-40 target examples Key validation question Identifiers patientid , sampleid , treatmentid Are patient, sample, and therapy records distinguishable? Disease cancer_type , tissueid , histo , stage What exact disease classification and source terminology were used? Demographics age , sex Are units and coding documented? Therapy treatment , target Is the drug/regimen and treatment context supported by the source? Outcome recist , response Is the definition of response and assessment timepoint explicit? Survival survival_time_os , event_occurred_os , survival_time_pfs , event_occurred_pfs , survival_unit Are time origin, endpoint definition, censoring and units confirmed? Assays rna , rna_info , dna , dna_info Is assay availability distinguished from assay type and processing method? For the complete current target schema and accepted values, use Data dictionary . Do not treat the example field list here as a replacement for the version-controlled dictionary. 5.3 Harmonization decision procedure For each source column: Retain the source column name and original values in a source-to-target mapping record. Confirm the source definition from the publication, metadata file, protocol, or data provider. Select a target MAR-40 variable only where the meanings align. Specify the transformation (rename, recode, unit conversion, join, derived value, or no mapping). Record the decision status: Direct , Conditional , Needs review , or Unmapped . Document the reviewer, date, and evidence for clinical/biological interpretation changes. Re-run checks after updating a mapping rule; never edit only the final exported table. Suggested mapping-log fields: cohort , source_file , source_variable , source_definition , target_variable , rule_id , transformation , mapping_status , evidence , reviewer , review_date , notes . 5.4 Cancer taxonomy and disease annotations Map source disease labels to the agreed OncoTree version. Maintain Level 1 cancer type as the shared broad classification and Level 2 subtype when known and supported. Retain the unmodified original tumor label and the exact mapping code/version. Ambiguous histology, multiple primaries, metastatic specimen labels, or unsupported subtype assignments must be flagged rather than inferred. 5.5 Treatment and response Immunotherapy categories include: PD-1/PD-L1 , CTLA4 , IO+combo , IO+chemo , and IO+targeted . Preserve original regimen and component drug names; use agreed MAR-40 categories only after recording a documented mapping. Combination categories require an explicit precedence or multi-label rule agreed by participating teams. Keep RECIST best response ( CR , PR , SD , PD , or evaluability status when supported) separate from binary responder/non-responder outcome. Do not derive binary response from RECIST unless the study-specific response definition and threshold are documented. Record the assessment system/version and response timepoint when available. 5.6 Survival endpoints Store OS and PFS times separately from their event indicators. Represent event values only after verifying the source's event/censoring convention (e.g. 1 = event, 0 = censored); never assume a coding direction. Use months for harmonized survival duration; preserve original units, the conversion method, and the agreed precision. Verify the time origin (diagnosis, treatment initiation, randomization, etc.). Do not pool survival measurements with incompatible or unknown origins without explicit analytical justification. Distinguish metadata availability (at least one nonmissing time or event field) from analysis readiness (a valid paired time/event record and a known endpoint definition). 6. Molecular data curation 6.1 Inventory available assay data The curation workflow covers processed RNA-seq counts/TPM, microarray expression, RNA-seq FASTQ, SNV mutation files, and CNA segment or matrix data. For each assay record the originating platform, sample IDs, reference genome, gene annotation, pipeline/tool versions, normalization, filtering, and quality metrics where available. 6.2 RNA expression Prefer source-supported normalized expression values and record their measurement scale. An example expression transformation is log2(TPM + 1) . This is an assay-specific processing option, not a universal conversion rule: confirm applicability and document the pseudocount, normalization method, and whether the values were already transformed. If deriving TPM from counts, use documented feature lengths appropriate to the quantification level and record the source of lengths. Do not apply the illustrative conversion without validating gene-length definitions and the input's count type. For microarrays, retain the platform, probe-to-gene mapping, and source normalization information; do not label microarray values as TPM. 6.3 Mutation and copy-number data Record mutation type (SNV/indel), input format (e.g. VCF, MAF, gene-by-sample calls), variant-calling provenance, genome build, and filtering. Record CNA data representation (segments, copy-number calls, or gene-level matrix), reference genome and mapping methods. Where a binary gene-by-sample matrix is generated, preserve the logic converting raw calls to binary values and retain exclusions/uncertainties. 6.4 Annotation versions Use consistent gene annotations across datasets whenever possible, following the MAR-40 harmonization strategy: GENCODE v19 : Default reference for published datasets when reprocessing raw data is not possible and the original annotation version is not specified. GENCODE v40 : Preferred reference for datasets with accessible raw data that can be reprocessed through the standardized pipeline. Source-specific annotations : When a publication or data provider explicitly reports the annotation version used, retain and document that version to preserve consistency with the original data. Record the annotation release, reference genome, gene identifier format, and processing method for each dataset. Any conversion between annotation versions, gene identifiers, or genome builds must be explicitly documented and traceable. Established gene, drug, and tumor annotation resources should be used consistently, with the corresponding resource versions recorded. 7. Build harmonized objects and link clinical/molecular data For R/Bioconductor workflows, supported integration objects include: SummarizedExperiment for expression or suitable feature-by-sample matrices. RangedSummarizedExperiment when genomic feature ranges are required. MultiAssayExperiment (MAE) to combine assays with clinical metadata and sample-to-patient links. Minimum structural checks: assay() feature/sample axes match rowData() and colData() ; each assay's sample IDs can be traced to the relevant patient; and sampleMap() relationships are checked rather than assumed. Maintain clear provenance when inputs differ by source, preprocessing or assay type. MAE should be considered a target integration representation , not a requirement to fabricate molecular assays for a clinical-only cohort. The exact MAR-40 output contract and filenames should be defined in Data dictionary and Usage . 8. Quality control and release gates Perform QC at source , post-harmonization , and integrated output stages. See Quality control for executable rules and any approved thresholds. QC area Required review File integrity Inputs readable, expected schema, source/version/checksum recorded. Identity Missing or duplicated IDs; conflicting patient fields; sample-to-patient joins. Vocabulary Unmapped disease, drug, assay, response and access labels. Clinical consistency Implausible ages, invalid time/event codes, contradictory dates or survival data. Assay integrity Feature IDs, sample IDs, annotation release, dimensions, build and measurement units. Completeness Missingness by cohort, field, patient/sample, and timepoint. Traceability Every derived field links to a documented source and rule/version. QC review dispositions: Pass: QC checks satisfied; all required provenance supplied. Pass with documented limitations: Missing or noncritical issues disclosed and approved by a reviewer. Hold for review: Clinically material mapping conflicts, unverifiable links, access concerns, or failed structural checks. Do not treat a simple cohort-level presence/absence heatmap as a full QC or survival-analysis readiness assessment. 9. Outputs, reproducibility, and handoff Suggested cohort handoff contents, subject to institutional permissions: \<cohort_id>/ ├── source_manifest.tsv # Source inventory, versions, permitted paths/checksums ├── mapping_log.tsv # Source -> MAR-40 transformations and decisions ├── clinical_harmonized.csv # Approved de-identified clinical metadata, if shareable ├── assay_manifest.tsv # Available assays and processing parameters ├── qc_summary.tsv # QC checks, results, exceptions ├── unresolved_issues.tsv # Items requiring reviewer decisions └── run_manifest.txt # Git commit, environment, execution parameters, date A molecular-data object (e.g. .rds MAE) may be produced in an approved destination when supported by the cohort and workflow. This is the recommended cohort handoff structure; include only files supported by the cohort and permitted by institutional access requirements. Capture the following run details: source file versions/checksums, approved execution location, Git commit, Pixi/other environment lockfile, workflow command, tool versions, mapping version, start date, curator and reviewer. Scripts should be rerunnable without hard-coded local machine paths; use paths/configuration described in Usage . Suggested submission review checklist [ ] Data sources, access permissions, and provenance are documented. [ ] Clinical metadata follow the MAR-40 standardized data dictionary. [ ] Patient and sample identifiers are consistent and correctly linked. [ ] Cancer types, treatments, response, and survival variables are harmonized according to the agreed definitions. [ ] Molecular data processing and annotation versions (e.g., GENCODE v19/v40) are documented. [ ] Clinical and molecular data are correctly integrated, including MAE validation where applicable. [ ] Quality-control checks are completed, and unresolved issues are documented. [ ] Harmonized outputs and processing steps are reproducible using version-controlled scripts. 10. Handling exceptions and SOP changes When a source requires a deviation, document the affected cohort, reason, alternative procedure, scientific impact, decision owner and approval date. Reusable deviations should be proposed as a versioned SOP or harmonization-rule update via repository review. Retain prior mapping versions so existing outputs remain interpretable. 11. Maintaining cross-site consistency The harmonization framework is shared across participating MAR-40 teams. Each site should use the current version of the Data dictionary , Data sources , Quality control , and Usage documentation when producing a cohort release. Changes to shared variable definitions, OncoTree classifications, treatment grouping, clinical endpoints, assay representations, QC criteria, or output formats must be recorded in version-controlled documentation and reviewed by the designated scientific/data leads before being applied across cohorts. Site-specific exceptions remain traceable in the mapping log and QC report. Changes affecting the interpretation of previously harmonized cohorts should trigger an assessment of whether existing outputs require regeneration. Preserve the source definitions, transformation rules, and previous output versions to support reproducibility. Document history Version Status Summary 1.0 Active MAR-40 cross-site data curation and harmonization SOP for UCL, McGill University, and UHN; includes source provenance, clinical and molecular harmonization, QC, and reproducibility procedures.

docs.text: Record mutation type (SNV/indel), input format (e.g. VCF, MAF, gene-by-sample calls), variant-calling provenance, genome build, and filtering. Record CNA data representation (segments, copy-number calls, or gene-level matrix), reference genome and mapping methods. Where a binary gene-by-sample matrix is generated, preserve the logic converting raw calls to binary values and retain exclusions/uncertainties.
docs.title: 6.3 Mutation and copy-number data

docs.text: Use consistent gene annotations across datasets whenever possible, following the MAR-40 harmonization strategy: GENCODE v19 : Default reference for published datasets when reprocessing raw data is not possible and the original annotation version is not specified. GENCODE v40 : Preferred reference for datasets with accessible raw data that can be reprocessed through the standardized pipeline. Source-specific annotations : When a publication or data provider explicitly reports the annotation version used, retain and document that version to preserve consistency with the original data. Record the annotation release, reference genome, gene identifier format, and processing method for each dataset. Any conversion between annotation versions, gene identifiers, or genome builds must be explicitly documented and traceable. Established gene, drug, and tumor annotation resources should be used consistently, with the corresponding resource versions recorded.
docs.title: 6.4 Annotation versions

docs.text: For R/Bioconductor workflows, supported integration objects include: SummarizedExperiment for expression or suitable feature-by-sample matrices. RangedSummarizedExperiment when genomic feature ranges are required. MultiAssayExperiment (MAE) to combine assays with clinical metadata and sample-to-patient links. Minimum structural checks: assay() feature/sample axes match rowData() and colData() ; each assay's sample IDs can be traced to the relevant patient; and sampleMap() relationships are checked rather than assumed. Maintain clear provenance when inputs differ by source, preprocessing or assay type. MAE should be considered a target integration representation , not a requirement to fabricate molecular assays for a clinical-only cohort. The exact MAR-40 output contract and filenames should be defined in Data dictionary and Usage .
docs.title: 7. Build harmonized objects and link clinical/molecular data

docs.text: Perform QC at source , post-harmonization , and integrated output stages. See Quality control for executable rules and any approved thresholds. QC area Required review File integrity Inputs readable, expected schema, source/version/checksum recorded. Identity Missing or duplicated IDs; conflicting patient fields; sample-to-patient joins. Vocabulary Unmapped disease, drug, assay, response and access labels. Clinical consistency Implausible ages, invalid time/event codes, contradictory dates or survival data. Assay integrity Feature IDs, sample IDs, annotation release, dimensions, build and measurement units. Completeness Missingness by cohort, field, patient/sample, and timepoint. Traceability Every derived field links to a documented source and rule/version. QC review dispositions: Pass: QC checks satisfied; all required provenance supplied. Pass with documented limitations: Missing or noncritical issues disclosed and approved by a reviewer. Hold for review: Clinically material mapping conflicts, unverifiable links, access concerns, or failed structural checks. Do not treat a simple cohort-level presence/absence heatmap as a full QC or survival-analysis readiness assessment.
docs.title: 8. Quality control and release gates

docs.text: Suggested cohort handoff contents, subject to institutional permissions: \<cohort_id>/ ├── source_manifest.tsv # Source inventory, versions, permitted paths/checksums ├── mapping_log.tsv # Source -> MAR-40 transformations and decisions ├── clinical_harmonized.csv # Approved de-identified clinical metadata, if shareable ├── assay_manifest.tsv # Available assays and processing parameters ├── qc_summary.tsv # QC checks, results, exceptions ├── unresolved_issues.tsv # Items requiring reviewer decisions └── run_manifest.txt # Git commit, environment, execution parameters, date A molecular-data object (e.g. .rds MAE) may be produced in an approved destination when supported by the cohort and workflow. This is the recommended cohort handoff structure; include only files supported by the cohort and permitted by institutional access requirements. Capture the following run details: source file versions/checksums, approved execution location, Git commit, Pixi/other environment lockfile, workflow command, tool versions, mapping version, start date, curator and reviewer. Scripts should be rerunnable without hard-coded local machine paths; use paths/configuration described in Usage .
docs.title: 9. Outputs, reproducibility, and handoff

docs.text: [ ] Data sources, access permissions, and provenance are documented. [ ] Clinical metadata follow the MAR-40 standardized data dictionary. [ ] Patient and sample identifiers are consistent and correctly linked. [ ] Cancer types, treatments, response, and survival variables are harmonized according to the agreed definitions. [ ] Molecular data processing and annotation versions (e.g., GENCODE v19/v40) are documented. [ ] Clinical and molecular data are correctly integrated, including MAE validation where applicable. [ ] Quality-control checks are completed, and unresolved issues are documented. [ ] Harmonized outputs and processing steps are reproducible using version-controlled scripts.
docs.title: Suggested submission review checklist

docs.text: When a source requires a deviation, document the affected cohort, reason, alternative procedure, scientific impact, decision owner and approval date. Reusable deviations should be proposed as a versioned SOP or harmonization-rule update via repository review. Retain prior mapping versions so existing outputs remain interpretable.
docs.title: 10. Handling exceptions and SOP changes

docs.text: The harmonization framework is shared across participating MAR-40 teams. Each site should use the current version of the Data dictionary , Data sources , Quality control , and Usage documentation when producing a cohort release. Changes to shared variable definitions, OncoTree classifications, treatment grouping, clinical endpoints, assay representations, QC criteria, or output formats must be recorded in version-controlled documentation and reviewed by the designated scientific/data leads before being applied across cohorts. Site-specific exceptions remain traceable in the mapping log and QC report. Changes affecting the interpretation of previously harmonized cohorts should trigger an assessment of whether existing outputs require regeneration. Preserve the source definitions, transformation rules, and previous output versions to support reproducibility.
docs.title: 11. Maintaining cross-site consistency

docs.text: Version Status Summary 1.0 Active MAR-40 cross-site data curation and harmonization SOP for UCL, McGill University, and UHN; includes source provenance, clinical and molecular harmonization, QC, and reproducibility procedures.

Proper documentation ensures reproducibility and helps others understand your research methodology. How to Document Your Data For each data source, include the following information: 1. External Data Sources Name : Official name of the dataset Version/Date : Version number or access date URL : Link to the data source Access Method : How the data was obtained (direct download, API, etc.) Access Date : When the data was accessed/retrieved Data Format : Format of the data (FASTQ, DICOM, CSV, etc.) Citation : Proper academic citation if applicable License : Usage restrictions and attribution requirements Example: ## TCGA RNA-Seq Data - **Name**: The Cancer Genome Atlas RNA-Seq Data - **Version**: Data release 28.0 - March 2021 - **URL**: https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/ - **Access Method**: GDC Data Transfer Tool - **Access Date**: 2021-03-15 - **Citation**: The Cancer Genome Atlas Network. (2012). Comprehensive molecular portraits of human breast tumours. Nature, 490(7418), 61-70. - **License**: [NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy](https://sharing.nih.gov/genomic-data-sharing-policy) 2. Internal/Generated Data Name : Descriptive name of the dataset Creation Date : When the data was generated Creation Method : Brief description of how the data was created Input Data : What source data was used Processing Scripts : References to scripts/Github Repo used to generate this data Example: ## Processed RNA-Seq Data - **Name**: Processed RNA-Seq Data for TCGA-BRCA - **Creation Date**: 2021-04-01 - **Creation Method**: Processed using kallisto and DESeq2 - **Input Data**: FASTQ Data obtained from the SRA database - **Processing Scripts**: [GitHub Repo](https://github.com/tcga-brca-rnaseq) 3. Data Dictionary For complex datasets, include a data dictionary that explains: Column Name Data Type Description Units Possible Values patient_id string Unique patient identifier N/A TCGA-XX-XXXX format age integer Patient age at diagnosis years 18-100 expression float Gene expression value TPM Any positive value Best Practices Store raw data in data/rawdata/ and never modify it Store processed data in data/procdata/ and all code used to generate it should be in workflow/scripts/ Document all processing steps Track data provenance (where data came from and how it was modified) Respect data usage agreements and licenses! This is especially important for data that should not be shared publicly

docs.text: Developer Notes Purpose of This Section This section is for documenting technical decisions, challenges, and solutions encountered during your project. These notes are valuable for: Future you (who will forget why certain decisions were made) Collaborators who join the project later People coming from your publication who want to reproduce your work Anyone who might want to extend your research What to Document Design Decisions Document important decisions about your project's architecture, algorithms, or methodologies: ## Choice of RNA-Seq Analysis Pipeline [2025-04-25] We chose the kallisto over STAR pipeline for the following reasons: 1. The CCLE dataset is very large, and kallisto is faster for quantifying large datasets 2. GDSC used kallisto, so we can compare our results with theirs Technical Challenges Record significant problems you encountered and how you solved them ## Sample Name Format Issue [2025-04-25] We encountered a problem with sample name formats between the CCLE and GDSC datasets. The CCLE dataset uses "BRCA-XX-XXXX" format, while the GDSC dataset uses "BRCA-XX-XXXX-XX". We had to write a script to remove the last two characters from the sample names in the GDSC dataset. Dependencies and Environment Document specific version requirements or compatibility issues: ## Critical Version Dependencies [2025-04-25] SimpleITK 2.4.1 introduced a bug that flips images, so we froze version 2.4.0 Best Practices Date your entries when appropriate Link to relevant code files or external resources Include small code snippets when helpful Note alternatives you considered and why they were rejected Document failed approaches to prevent others from repeating mistakes Update notes when major changes are made to the approach
